title: Chapter 23: Secure and Robust Java Development
description: Integrate security into ordinary design and review. Learners threat-model assets and entry points, prevent injection with structured APIs, constrain paths and parsers, handle secrets and passwords with approved facilities, enforce CPU, memory, time, queue, and output limits, and maintain dependency, configuration, patch, and audit evidence suitable for production ownership.

exercises.title: Chapter 23 implementation lab: redact
exercises.instructionMarkdown:
Implement `redact`. For secrets longer than four characters return *** plus the final four; otherwise return ***. Write the precondition and boundary table first, keep the method deterministic, and do not print.

Input is non-null. This masking rule is a practice contract; real logs should usually omit credentials entirely.
hints: Decide the length boundary first: secrets of four characters or fewer must be fully masked, and only longer secrets reveal a trailing slice.
Check both an empty string and a secret exactly at the four-character boundary before trusting the substring math for longer inputs.

exercises.title: Redact the entire short secret
exercises.instructionMarkdown: The supplied condition treats a secret up to and including four characters as safe to print unmasked, but a short secret must be fully redacted like any other. Repair the comparison so the program writes exactly `***`. Preserve the demonstrated redaction logic and explain why your fix changes the result; do not replace it with a hard-coded print. Output tests verify the result; preserving the intended redaction behavior requires source review.
hints: Short secrets must never be logged in full.

exercises.title: Portfolio checkpoint: hashed credential store
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement CredentialStore.run(String input) as the pure decision core behind the Authentication & User Management System project. Each nonblank trimmed line is one command; blank lines are skipped and produce no output line. REGISTER|username|password requires username to match [A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20} and not already be registered, and password to be at least 8 characters; on success it must store the password hashed with a real, salted algorithm (for example PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 via javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory, with a random salt per user) and never the plaintext, then print OK; otherwise ERROR. LOGIN|username|password prints OK only if the username exists and the password verifies against its stored hash, otherwise ERROR; never compare against a stored plaintext value. CHANGE|username|oldPassword|newPassword requires the username to exist, oldPassword to verify against the current stored hash, and newPassword to be at least 8 characters; on success it replaces the stored hash (with a fresh salt) and prints OK; otherwise ERROR, leaving the stored credential unchanged. Output is one line per nonblank input line, joined with \n, no trailing newline. Grading checks only this observable OK/ERROR behavior; source review separately confirms a real salted hash algorithm was actually used and that no plaintext password or hash ever appears in an exception message or log line.
hints: Two REGISTER calls with the identical password should still store two different-looking hashes if you inspect them directly (different random salts) — the grader only checks LOGIN behavior, but a source reviewer will check this.
A wrong oldPassword in CHANGE must reject the whole call, even if newPassword would otherwise be valid.

exercises.title: Portfolio checkpoint: role-gated task board
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement TaskBoard.run(String input) as the pure decision core behind the Project Management App project. Each nonblank trimmed line is one command; blank lines are skipped and produce no output line. TEAM|teamId|owner requires teamId to match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,20} and not already exist; creates the team with owner as its first member holding role OWNER; prints OK or ERROR. JOIN|teamId|member|role requires teamId to exist, role to be exactly OWNER or MEMBER, and member to not already belong to teamId; prints OK or ERROR. TASK|teamId|taskId|creator requires teamId to exist, creator to already be a member of teamId, and taskId to match the id pattern and not already exist (globally); creates the task with its assignee set to creator; prints OK or ERROR. ASSIGN|taskId|actor|assignee requires taskId to exist, assignee to be a member of the task's team, and actor to be either an OWNER of that team or the task's current assignee; on success sets the new assignee and prints OK, otherwise ERROR without changing the assignment. REMOVEMEMBER|teamId|actor|target requires teamId to exist, actor to be an OWNER of teamId, and target to currently be a member of teamId; prints OK and removes target, or ERROR otherwise. Output is one line per nonblank input line, joined with \n, no trailing newline. This models only the per-resource, role-dependent authorization core; a real app's notifications and due-date events are external, ungraded scope.
